## Per-chapter highlights

### Chapter 1 — After the Death of Joshua: The Incomplete Conquest, Tribe by Tribe

*status:* published
*themes:* covenant, judgment, prophetic-call

The book opens "after the death of Joshua." Israel asks who shall go up first; the LORD says Judah, who enlists Simeon and conducts a substantial southern campaign — Adonibezek, Jerusalem, Hebron, Othniel's capture of Debir (Josh 15:16-19 replayed) — until iron chariots block the valley. The chapter then extends Joshua's localized territorial-incomplete notations into a tribe-by-tribe pattern of failure across Benjamin, Manasseh, Ephraim, Zebulun, Asher, Naphtali, and Dan.

### Chapter 2 — Bochim — Joshua's Death Recalled — the Cyclic-Pattern Installed

*status:* published
*themes:* covenant, judgment, prophetic-call

An angel of the LORD comes up from Gilgal to Bochim and delivers a covenantal-lawsuit — Israel was to make no league with the inhabitants nor leave their altars, but did so; therefore the nations will remain as thorns in Israel's sides and their gods a snare. The people weep, sacrifice, and name the place "Weepers." The chapter then recalls Joshua's death and notes that another generation arose "which knew not the LORD." The cyclic-pattern programmatic statement at 2:11-23 installs the book's interpretive key: evil → oppression → cry → judge → rest → renewed evil.

### Chapter 3 — Othniel — Ehud — Shamgar: Three Judges, the First Cycles Executed

*status:* published
*themes:* covenant, judgment, deliverance, prophetic-call

The remnant-nations the LORD left "to prove Israel" are named; the cyclic-pattern installed at Judges 2 begins its narrative execution. Othniel — Caleb's younger brother, the figure who closed Joshua's southern campaign and now closes the Joshua-to-Judges bridge — is the framework's compressed-clean first iteration (40 years of rest). Ehud the left-handed Benjamite delivers Israel from Eglon king of Moab via covert-assassination (80 years of rest, double Othniel's), and Shamgar's one-verse notation closes the chapter — six hundred Philistines slain with an ox goad.

### Chapter 4 — Deborah and Barak — Sisera at Kishon — Jael at the Tent

*status:* published
*themes:* covenant, judgment, deliverance, prophetic-call

Israel returns to evil after Ehud's death; Jabin king of Canaan oppresses with nine hundred chariots of iron. Deborah the prophetess summons Barak from Kedesh-naphtali, conveys the LORD's battle-plan at the river Kishon, and — when Barak asks her to come — prophesies that the LORD will sell Sisera "into the hand of a woman." The battle goes Israel's way; Sisera flees on foot to the tent of Jael wife of Heber the Kenite, who drives a tent- peg through his temples while he sleeps — the prophecy's literal fulfillment and the iron-chariots framework's narrative-resolution at Kishon.

### Chapter 5 — The Song of Deborah: Hebrew Poetry's Witness to the Kishon Victory

*status:* published
*themes:* covenant, judgment, deliverance, prophetic-call

Deborah and Barak sing the deliverance — preamble + Sinai- theophany imagery (5:1-5); pre-Deborah desolation and her rise as "a mother in Israel" (5:6-8); the tribal participation roll- call naming who came and who did not (5:9-18); the cosmic- battle at Megiddo with the stars in their courses fighting against Sisera and the river of Kishon sweeping them away (5:19-22); the curse of Meroz + the Jael celebration as the song's centerpiece (5:23-27); the mother of Sisera at the window waiting in vain + the closing curse-and-blessing benediction (5:28-31).

### Chapter 9 — Abimelech at Shechem — Jotham's Parable — the Curse Fulfilled

*status:* published
*themes:* covenant, judgment, prophetic-call

Abimelech, Gideon's son by the Shechem concubine, takes seventy pieces of silver from the house of Baalberith and slays his seventy brothers on one stone — all but Jotham, who hides. From Mount Gerizim Jotham delivers the parable of the trees and pronounces a conditional curse. After three years God sends an evil spirit between Abimelech and Shechem; Gaal's revolt fails, Abimelech burns Shechem and the tower of Shechem, and dies at Thebez when a woman drops a millstone on his head — the closure- formula names the rendering and Jotham's curse fulfilled.
